topic:
Sharp unknown-history minimax frontier for globally stable longitudinal incremental interventions. For all integers n>=1,T>=1 and known c in [0,1], observe n iid complete trajectories O=(X1,A1,...,XT,AT,Y), all Xt and At binary and Y in [0,1]. Let Ht=(X1,A1,...,X_(t-1),A_(t-1),Xt). The law class P_T includes every trajectory law on this sample space, with arbitrary history-dependent covariate, action and outcome kernels. For causal interpretation impose consistency and sequential exchangeability (no hidden treatment confounding); no missingness, Markov, smoothness, sparsity or positive treatment-probability floor is imposed. The data analyst knows n,T,c and the alphabet, and is not supplied any true kernel. Define pi_t(Ht)=P(At=1|Ht), eta=c/sqrt(T), delta=exp(eta), and q_t(P)(1|Ht)=delta*pi_t/[1+(delta-1)*pi_t]. Replace all action kernels by q_t(P), retaining covariate/outcome kernels. Let psi_T(P,c) be the resulting terminal mean. This intervened law is dominated by P, so conditional versions on P-null histories do not change psi. Deterministic treatment and null histories are included. Determine explicit evaluable functions r(n,T,c) and ell(n,T,c), up to universal multiplicative constants independent of n,T,c, for R(n,T,c)=inf_{all measurable estimators} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[(hatpsi-psi_T(P,c))^2] and L(n,T,c)=inf_{I} sup_{P in P_T} E_P[length(I)], where I is a measurable connected interval in [0,1], with optional independent randomization, satisfying inf_{P in P_T} P_P(psi_T(P,c) in I)>=0.95. Prove matching upper and lower bounds uniformly for every n,T,c, including saturation, shrinking c, and all logarithmic transition factors. Upper results must supply total finite-data algorithms for an estimator and such an interval, with stated computational cost; converses range over all estimators/intervals on the original iid experiment and the same P_T. Derive necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform consistency along sequences T=T_n,c=c_n and characterize exactly when knowing the complete propensity tree changes the order of risk or honest length. At c=0 recover R of order 1/n and L of order 1/sqrt(n). The known-propensity benchmark is uniformly order 1/n and 1/sqrt(n) for all T,c in the domain. Whether or where unknown propensities create a strict penalty is answer-open, not assumed. Exact rates, transitions, estimator algebra and proof mechanics are outputs. A fixed-T EIF, oracle-only bound, unmatched rate bracket, or illustrative impossibility example does not satisfy the kernel. Consumer: Kim, Kennedy and Naimi, Incremental Intervention Effects in Studies with Dropout and Many Timepoints (2021), analyze EAGeR aspirin adherence and pregnancy across many weeks; the mtpverse/imtp software implements incremental interventions with learned treatment propensities. The theorem would establish whether increasing the history length requires more subjects or structural restrictions even when the oracle weights have bounded second moment, informing how these workflows justify estimation precision for long histories. This binary, completely observed experiment is an explicitly restricted theoretical benchmark, not a numerical sample-size prescription for their richer covariate/dropout analysis. Sources https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.04004 and https://github.com/mtpverse/imtp . PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A bounded presolve derived more than the known-propensity variance calculation. Complement-paired context priors make every deterministic-history intervention mean exactly one-half, while randomized late actions shift a majority outcome. Their observed-data mixtures agree whenever sampled contexts occupy different pairs, producing a sparse-history lower mechanism without random-target concentration. A natural-mean estimator with an explicit deterministic intervention-bias envelope supplies a matching long-history upper route. The full-law influence function also has a dimension-independent second-moment bound, separating local efficiency from uniform sparse-history difficulty. Independent finite enumeration checked the paired-target identity, nonuniform early intervention weights, and small-mixture likelihoods; finite differences checked the influence formula. These checks are not proofs of uniform bounds or the full frontier. Deterministic actions, null histories, zero and shrinking intervention strength, and recent static incremental/OPE comparators were considered.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Close the sharp intermediate-history transition through a compatible prefix-probability approximation/variance theorem and matching all-procedure converse, including connected honest-interval length; endpoint results must not replace this requirement.
EARLY KILL TEST: Audit the k=1,r=2 paired model and two-action prefix functional: verify mixture indistinguishability, shifted pair cancellation, and nonidentity with a static tilt, then identify the first mixed-prefix correction absent from prior theorems. Stop and re-gate if the witness fails or an existing exact reduction supplies the entire frontier.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_incremental_history_learning_frontier.md

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp all-sample minimax MSE frontier for a terminal longitudinal odds-multiplier intervention with delta=exp(c/sqrt(T)) when the complete binary propensity tree is unknown and no positivity, Markov, smoothness, or sparsity restriction is imposed.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives identification, an EIF, and nuisance-rate inference, but its growing-horizon result is an IPW variance comparison under a common constant propensity rather than a global minimax theorem.
source_refs.author: Kwangho Kim, Edward H. Kennedy, Ashley I. Naimi

source_refs.claim: Natural stochastic policies have an inflated efficiency bound because the evaluation policy depends on the unknown behavior policy, but the paper gives local asymptotic rather than unrestricted finite-sample minimax theory.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Finite-action bandit OPE exhibits a sharp finite-sample separation between known and unknown behavior policies, with polynomial approximation needed in low-exploration regimes.
source_refs.author: Cong Ma, Banghua Zhu, Jiantao Jiao, Martin J. Wainwright

source_refs.claim: Single-exposure minimax lower bounds show that local EIF calculations need not exhaust the global tilt-dependent difficulty of incremental effects.
source_refs.author: Kyle Schindl, Shuying Shen, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.excerpt: Adaptation, approximate state sufficiency, and longer horizons remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi analyze fixed-T efficient estimation and a special constant-propensity growing-T variance comparison, while Kallus and Uehara establish only local efficiency for natural policies. Neither controls the global cost of learning an exponentially branching history-indexed propensity law. Bandit minimax theory is one-stage with a fixed target policy, whereas here q_t(P) is a nonlinear function of the unknown behavior propensity and compounds along random histories. The archived g-formula project also stops at two decisions under overlap and Hölder restrictions; its fixed-dimensional projection step must be replaced by an occupancy-sensitive prefix representation valid for null histories and more histories than observations. The presolve's paired-mixture mechanism remains a hypothesis until its k=1,r=2 cancellation and first mixed-prefix correction are proved.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit evaluable r(n,T,c), including saturation and all transition factors, together with a total finite-data estimator attaining risk O(r) and an all-measurable-estimator lower bound of order r uniformly for every n,T,c.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from positivity-robust longitudinal estimands to the practical many-timepoint precision question, replacing its special-case variance comparison by a global decision-theoretic frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Dense longitudinal studies create long histories and fragile positivity -> incremental interventions remain identified without treatment positivity -> local efficiency suggests stable oracle weights -> determine whether learning unrestricted histories nevertheless creates a finite-sample minimax penalty

method_exemplars.technique: Combine switching, low-occupancy polynomial approximation, and behavior-policy mixture lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Trajectory prefixes act like sparsely sampled arms, but the proof must additionally handle a target weight determined by those same unknown probabilities.

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order influence-function corrections with projection kernels and degenerate-U-statistic bias-variance analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery can convert products of longitudinal nuisance errors into an attainable non-root-n rate once fixed-dimensional projections are replaced by prefix-occupancy operators.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate Le Cam alternatives using tilt-dependent functional separation and likelihood-ratio moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly connects an incremental estimand's tilt to global difficulty, although one exposure must be replaced by a learned random prefix product.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a tree-structured polynomial or factorial-moment estimator for the propensity-dependent incremental mean and determine whether it attains the sharp intermediate-history minimax transition under arbitrary prefix masses, null histories, and unequal unknown propensities.

source_refs.claim: A Chebyshev-polynomial estimator is required for minimax OPE in a low-exploration bandit regime where ordinary plug-in estimation is suboptimal.
source_refs.author: Cong Ma, Banghua Zhu, Jiantao Jiao, Martin J. Wainwright

source_refs.claim: Best-polynomial approximations estimated by factorial moments attain minimax rates for large-alphabet functionals in low-count regions.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Kartik Venkat, Yanjun Han, Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.claim: The longitudinal identifying functional and EIF are available, but no estimator learns arbitrary history-dependent propensity cells with a uniform all-n minimax guarantee.
source_refs.author: Kwangho Kim, Edward H. Kennedy, Ashley I. Naimi

source_refs.excerpt: The bound permits unknown unequal propensities, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, null cells
the same unknown cell mass determines both its sampling intensity and its weight in the target law

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor polynomial constructions estimate additive scalar functionals of unrelated multinomial cells or one-stage values under fixed targets. A trajectory tree is not a flat alphabet: child masses sum to parent masses, each conditional propensity enters both the observed likelihood and q_t(P), and errors propagate through downstream prefixes. The first proof step that changes is the scalar Poissonized unbiased-moment representation, which must become a compatible prefix recursion with a covariance theorem for nested counts. Searches combining polynomial approximation with longitudinal incremental interventions located only the donor large-alphabet and bandit results, not this target-method pair. Moreover, the presolve's complement-paired witness must first pass the stipulated k=1,r=2 identity, cancellation, and non-static-tilt checks.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A proved k=1,r=2 audit followed by a total prefix-recursive polynomial estimator with explicit degree and truncation schedules, uniform bias-variance bounds giving a closed-form intermediate-regime rate, and a matching multinomial-mixture or moment-matching converse.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its longitudinal incremental formulation and application-facing motivation; present the polynomial papers only as technique donors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Incremental odds shifts define a support-respecting longitudinal target -> arbitrary histories form a huge sparse propensity tree -> standard EIF nuisance conditions do not control unseen prefixes -> reconstruct their aggregate contribution with a minimax finite-data procedure

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Chebyshev approximation and unbiased factorial moments under Poissonization to low-probability behavior-policy contributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the unknown-logging low-occupancy problem for one-stage OPE; the required extension couples contributions across prefixes.

method_exemplars.technique: Split smooth and nonsmooth probability regions, estimate best polynomials unbiasedly in the latter, and derive matching lower bounds through approximation-moment duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rare-prefix bias is structurally analogous to unseen-symbol bias, but the approximation must respect tree compatibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Implement higher-order causal corrections with empirical projection operators and control their U-statistic remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a causal route from polynomial nuisance approximation to an implementable estimator and limit theory.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly, along every sequence (n,T_n,c_n), when supplying the complete true propensity tree strictly improves the order of minimax MSE or honest confidence-interval length for longitudinal incremental interventions.

source_refs.claim: For natural stochastic policies, unknown behavior propensities inflate the semiparametric efficiency bound but leave its horizon order unchanged under the paper's assumptions.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Unknown behavior policies incur a support-size finite-sample competitive penalty in bandit OPE despite plug-in asymptotic optimality.
source_refs.author: Cong Ma, Banghua Zhu, Jiantao Jiao, Martin J. Wainwright

source_refs.claim: For the single-time ATE, weighting with a nonparametrically estimated propensity can attain the efficiency bound, so knowing the true score need not improve first-order precision.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano, Guido W. Imbens, Geert Ridder

source_refs.claim: Estimating longer-history behavior policies can lower asymptotic variance while increasing finite-sample bias, exposing a history-length bias-variance tension.
source_refs.author: Hongyi Zhou, Josiah P. Hanna, Jin Zhu, Ying Yang, Chengchun Shi

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature points in three different directions: estimating a propensity can improve or preserve first-order efficiency, natural-policy dependence can inflate but not change the order of a local efficiency bound, and finite-support minimax theory can produce a large unknown-policy penalty. None treats a target q(P) that changes with the unknown propensity itself, exponentially many possible prefixes, and a local per-period shift c/sqrt(T). Therefore neither semiparametric efficiency nor fixed-target support size identifies the global regime in which oracle propensity information changes the order of risk or honest length.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient regime theorem, expressed by explicit inequalities in n,T,c or an equivalent effective-prefix complexity, separating order-equivalence from strict separation of the unknown- and known-propensity minimax risks and honest lengths, with exact coincidence at c=0.

writing_exemplar.why: Its introduction is organized around the precise finite-sample question of whether knowing the behavior policy helps.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Plug-in behavior-policy estimation can look oracle-optimal asymptotically -> sparse finite samples can reverse that conclusion -> longitudinal prefixes create a growing implicit action alphabet -> locate the exact oracle-gap phase diagram for an endogenous incremental policy

method_exemplars.technique: Compare behavior-known switch estimators with behavior-unknown plug-in procedures through sparse-distribution competitive-ratio lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly formalizes the oracle-information comparison, with prefixes replacing arms and q(P) requiring a new coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit estimated-score calibration to project out nuisance variation and attain the semiparametric bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the canonical no-oracle-gain mechanism that any claimed penalty must reconcile with at one timepoint and at c=0.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive and attain separate efficiency bounds for fixed and behavior-dependent stochastic policies using compatible nuisance estimates and a second-order remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the direct local comparison for propensity-dependent policies whose global finite-sample analogue is sought.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimax expected length of 95% honest connected confidence intervals for the unknown-history longitudinal incremental mean, uniformly over all n,T,c and including rare-prefix and saturation regimes.

source_refs.claim: Its uniform inference uses asymptotic Gaussian-process approximation and nuisance convergence conditions; the growing-horizon result does not establish finite-sample honesty or optimal expected length.
source_refs.author: Kwangho Kim, Edward H. Kennedy, Ashley I. Naimi

source_refs.claim: CoinDICE provides behavior-agnostic OPE intervals but assumes an MDP/function-embedding formulation and does not characterize minimax expected connected length.
source_refs.author: Bo Dai, Ofir Nachum, Yinlam Chow, Lihong Li, Csaba Szepesvari, Dale Schuurmans

source_refs.claim: Expected-length lower bounds for honest intervals are characterized through between-class ordered moduli in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low

source_refs.excerpt: unseen categories produce an additional \(d/[n\log(en)]\) uncertainty term
broader longitudinal or flexible-covariate extensions remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-T EIF/Wald or bootstrap validity under nuisance-rate assumptions does not imply finite-sample honesty over a trajectory simplex whose dimension grows exponentially and includes zero-probability histories. Prior discrete-ATE and threshold-LMTP work supplies rare-cell radii or bias-aware fallbacks only for one-stage targets. In the longitudinal problem, the confidence-radius decomposition must become prefix-compatible and control endogenous intervention weights without a union bound over exponentially many histories. CoinDICE's Bellman constraints are unavailable without Markov structure, and no cited work supplies an all-randomized-procedure expected-length converse for this nonlinear target.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit ell(n,T,c), a total algorithm returning a connected interval in [0,1] with coverage at least 0.95 for every law and worst-case expected length O(ell), and a matching lower bound over every possibly randomized honest connected interval.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its many-timepoint application motivation and emphasis on uniform inference, while distinguishing asymptotic nuisance-controlled guarantees from finite-sample honesty.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Incremental interventions support long-horizon analyses without treatment positivity -> applications require uncertainty, not only point estimates -> unrestricted growing histories defeat fixed-T Gaussian approximations -> find the shortest uniformly honest connected interval

method_exemplars.technique: Lower-bound expected length with ordered moduli and invert affine tests to construct intervals within constants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired ell is also an expected-length optimization under uniform coverage, with iid trajectory-mixture affinity replacing Gaussian distance.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn behavior-agnostic distribution-correction equations into generalized empirical-likelihood endpoint programs with finite-sample control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a computational interval pattern for unknown logging policies, but the equations must be rebuilt for an endogenous non-Markov target.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine explicit worst-case bias accounting with modulus-based confidence-length lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sparse-prefix bias must be incorporated at the same scale as the stochastic radius rather than treated as asymptotically negligible.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an adaptive prefix-depth Rao-Blackwellized estimator for the unknown-history incremental mean and prove an oracle inequality and matching converse identifying the optimal retained depth in the intermediate-T regime.

source_refs.claim: Conditional Monte Carlo explains when marginalized importance sampling reduces horizon dependence and shows that finite-horizon variance reduction is not automatic.
source_refs.author: Yao Liu, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Emma Brunskill

source_refs.claim: Sequential doubly robust OPE combines importance weighting and value regression and can match a hardness lower bound in certain finite-horizon settings.
source_refs.author: Nan Jiang, Lihong Li

source_refs.claim: Double reinforcement learning attains semiparametric efficiency using marginalized density ratios, explicitly relying on Markov state compression.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Masatoshi Uehara

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditional and marginalized importance sampling assume exact or estimable conditional ratios for a fixed target, while Markov DRL compresses histories into observed states. Here no exact state compression exists and q_t(P) changes when the behavior propensity estimate changes. Consequently, conditioning on a shorter prefix introduces both ordinary approximation bias and an endogenous-target mixed-prefix correction. Targeted searches located fixed-policy horizon-variance and fixed-T incremental-EIF results, but no data-driven prefix selector with a global minimax guarantee. The first proof step is an exact prefix-conditioning identity isolating that correction before any Lepski or aggregation argument can apply.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A prefix-depth-indexed estimator family, a uniform decomposition into sampling variance, omitted-history error, and endogenous-target correction, a data-driven selector attaining the best depth up to stated logarithms, and an all-estimator lower bound matching the optimized expression.

writing_exemplar.why: Keep the motivation centered on incremental interventions and use conditional OPE solely as the donor technique for the intermediate-history bottleneck.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full-history incremental weights are formally bounded -> learning every history cell is unstable as T grows -> prefix conditioning offers a graded bias-variance tradeoff -> identify the exact adaptive depth and its minimax transition

method_exemplars.technique: Represent marginalized and per-decision importance sampling as conditional Monte Carlo projections and bound their horizon-dependent variances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Prefix truncation is a nested conditional-projection problem, but the new theorem must add approximation bias and propensity-target feedback.

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively augment sequential importance weights with value regressions and compare the resulting variance to an information lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its stagewise recursion is the closest estimator algebra for inserting a mixed-prefix correction while retaining bounded outcomes.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit value functions and marginalized density ratios, control their product remainder, and identify the efficient variance under state compression.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Retained prefix depth acts like a deliberately imperfect state representation whose approximation error must be quantified rather than assumed away.

open_problems.open_problem: Locate the sharp local transition in minimax risk and honest length as the global odds-shift strength c=c_n shrinks while the unrestricted history horizon T=T_n grows.

source_refs.excerpt: determine the sharp cardinality-uniform order of \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,1+\delta_T)\)

open_problems.why_unsolved: The POMDP proposal exposes an endpoint-versus-fixed-radius discontinuity but explicitly leaves its shrinking-radius transition unresolved. For incremental interventions the analogous local parameter is c: c=0 gives the natural mean, while c/sqrt(T) can accumulate over T decisions. The donor construction cannot be reapplied verbatim because the data are iid complete trajectories rather than one dependent partially observed process. Its observed-filter KL argument must be replaced by an iid trajectory-mixture affinity calculation tracking how paired-prefix cancellation degrades at the first mixed prefix. The presolve evidence for this cancellation is unverified and cannot yet be treated as a theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient phase diagram for sequences T_n,c_n, expressed through explicit r(n,T,c) and ell(n,T,c), that proves the c=0 parametric endpoint and identifies every crossover where accumulated unknown-propensity uncertainty changes consistency, risk, or honest length.

writing_exemplar.why: Its many-timepoint variance discussion supplies the destination framing for how a small per-visit intervention accumulates with horizon.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Incremental effects permit small support-respecting changes -> a per-visit shift of c/sqrt(T) is globally stable -> zero shift is the ordinary sample mean -> determine exactly how quickly nonzero accumulated intervention difficulty appears

method_exemplars.technique: Balance history-dependent bias against weight variance and localize testing alternatives under a shrinking policy-distance parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a proof template for a horizon-by-local-shift transition, although its dependent hidden-state experiment must be replaced.

method_exemplars.technique: Use two-convex-mixture lower bounds calibrated by functional separation and product-law affinity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The local-c frontier needs observed mixtures that remain close while the propensity-dependent intervention mean separates at a c- and T-dependent scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand the exact longitudinal odds-shift identifying functional uniformly around delta=1.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the target algebra whose local expansion determines how the intervention departs from the natural mean.

literature_map:
Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi (2021, JCI; arXiv:1907.04004) is the closest causal anchor: it gives identification, EIFs, nuisance-rate inference, and the many-timepoint application.
Its growing-horizon calculation compares IPW variances under a common constant propensity; it is not a global minimax analysis over arbitrary history trees.
Kennedy (2019, JASA; arXiv:1704.00211) establishes positivity-free binary incremental-intervention identification and fixed-T efficiency theory.
Kallus and Uehara (2024, Biometrika; arXiv:2006.03886) show that unknown-policy dependence inflates natural-policy efficiency bounds while preserving their order under structured models.
Ma, Zhu, Jiao, and Wainwright (2022, IEEE TIT; arXiv:2101.07781) establish a finite-sample known-versus-unknown logging-policy gap and a sparse-regime Chebyshev estimator.
Li, Munos, and Szepesvari (2015, AISTATS; arXiv:1409.3653) give a foundational unseen-action minimax decomposition for finite OPE.
Wang, Agarwal, and Dudik (2017, ICML; arXiv:1612.01205) show contextual richness contributes an additional agnostic OPE minimax term.
Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015, IEEE TIT; arXiv:1406.6956) supply the best-polynomial and factorial-moment machinery for rare discrete cells.
Jiang and Li (2016, ICML; arXiv:1511.03722) provide sequential doubly robust estimator algebra and matching hardness examples.
Kallus and Uehara (2020, JMLR; arXiv:1908.08526) attain efficient OPE through Markov state compression and marginalized ratios, structure absent here.
Liu, Bacon, and Brunskill (2020, ICML; arXiv:1910.06508) show by conditional Monte Carlo that horizon variance reduction is not automatic.
Schindl, Shen, and Kennedy (2024; arXiv:2409.11967) show for one exposure that tilt-dependent global difficulty can exceed what local EIF calculations reveal.
Zhou, Hanna, Zhu, Yang, and Shi (2025, ICML; arXiv:2505.22492) expose a longer-history tradeoff between reduced asymptotic variance and increased finite-sample bias from estimating behavior policies.
Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003, Econometrica) provide the opposing single-time phenomenon that estimating the propensity can attain the efficiency bound.
CoinDICE, off-policy confidence-sequence work, and Cai-Low modulus theory supply interval techniques, but none gives minimax expected connected length for an unrestricted propensity-dependent longitudinal target.

Mined the rejected two-period g-formula core for its explicit longer-horizon boundary and unresolved sequential-HOIF remainder.
Inspected the g-formula angle reviews; they emphasize rank-stable projection when basis dimension exceeds sample size.
Mined the accepted Jackson-factorial optimal-value run for its null-cell, unequal-propensity estimator and moment-matching converse.
Mined the downgraded discrete CATE-law run for the coupled unknown-mass and sampling-intensity obstruction.
Mined the discrete-ATE honest-inference run for heavy-light factorial confidence radii and unseen-category expected-length penalties.
Mined the accepted threshold-LMTP README; its result is one-stage and explicitly leaves broader longitudinal extensions open.

The failed sequential second-order and off-policy Fourier runs were also inspected, but their constructions were less directly transferable than the retained opportunities.
